<p class="project-page-intro">
LLM inference runtimes, GPU kernels, compiler performance analysis, and edge deployment.
Featured results include their workload and baseline so each measurement has context.
</p>

## Featured Systems Work

<div class="featured-project-grid">
  <a class="featured-project-card" href="https://github.com/AmanPandey28/cross_dsl_kernels" target="_blank" rel="noopener">
    <span class="featured-project-kicker">GPU Kernel Engineering</span>
    <span class="featured-project-title">GPU Kernel Optimization for LLM Inference</span>
    <span class="featured-project-description">
      FP32 RMSNorm and GEMV/small-M GEMM in CUDA C++ and Triton on RTX 5050.
      Residual-add/RMSNorm fusion reduced seven eager PyTorch launches to one at
      256 × 4096; passed 80/80 backend-shape checks against PyTorch.
    </span>
    <span class="featured-project-footer">15.3–16.3× vs. earlier M=16 Triton projections · CUDA Graph medians</span>
  </a>

  <a class="featured-project-card" href="https://github.com/AmanPandey28/nano_vllm_pp" target="_blank" rel="noopener">
    <span class="featured-project-kicker">Inference Runtime</span>
    <span class="featured-project-title">nano-vLLM: Single-GPU LLM Runtime</span>
    <span class="featured-project-description">
      Token-budget continuous batching, chunked prefill, paged KV tables, and
      prefix caching with OpenAI-style serving. On 12 mixed-length Qwen3-0.6B
      requests, output throughput rose from 58 to 223 tokens/s versus single-sequence scheduling.
    </span>
    <span class="featured-project-footer">3.84× throughput · Prefix reuse: median TTFT 139 → 34 ms</span>
  </a>

  <a class="featured-project-card" href="https://github.com/AmanPandey28/torch-compile-internals" target="_blank" rel="noopener">
    <span class="featured-project-kicker">Compiler &amp; Performance Analysis</span>
    <span class="featured-project-title">PyTorch Compiler &amp; LLM Inference</span>
    <span class="featured-project-description">
      FX capture, torch.cond, fusion analysis, and correctness-gated benchmarks
      with isolated caches and fresh-process profiling on RTX 5050. Investigated
      both pointwise speedups and a compiled MLP latency regression.
    </span>
    <span class="featured-project-footer">Qwen2.5-0.5B FP32: 8-step decode 97.9 → 66.8 ms · CUDA Graphs off</span>
  </a>

  <a class="featured-project-card" href="https://github.com/AmanPandey28/triton-flash-attention" target="_blank" rel="noopener">
    <span class="featured-project-kicker">Attention Kernels</span>
    <span class="featured-project-title">Triton FlashAttention-2: Forward Attention</span>
    <span class="featured-project-description">
      FA2-style forward attention with online softmax, FP16 MHA/GQA, and causal
      tile pruning. Passed 60/60 CUDA cases against PyTorch SDPA with maximum
      absolute output error 2.44 × 10<sup>−4</sup>.
    </span>
    <span class="featured-project-footer">1.15× vs. eager SDPA · Causal B=1, H=16, N=511, D=64 · RTX 5050</span>
  </a>

  <a class="featured-project-card" href="https://github.com/AmanPandey28/lpcv2026" target="_blank" rel="noopener">
    <span class="featured-project-kicker">Edge AI · LPCVC 2026</span>
    <span class="featured-project-title">MobileCLIP2 on Qualcomm QNN</span>
    <span class="featured-project-description">
      Static PyTorch → ONNX → QNN deployment of MobileCLIP2-S2, with FastViT
      reparameterization and preprocessing corrections. Validated all 56 image
      and 211 text device outputs at unchanged R@10 of 0.897470.
    </span>
    <span class="featured-project-footer">Image/text P90: 14.51/3.99 ms · S22 Family · 794/794 profiled ops on NPU</span>
  </a>
</div>
